Author: dajoey
Name: LazyCrucible
Description: For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Fills the ten-familiar run roster at the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu and the three Battlehorn slots before every fight with the familiars that answer that fight's mechanics: elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses and crowd control, skipping knocked-out familiars and benching badly hurt ones. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.
Punchline: Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight
Changelog:
v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.11 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction now waits for the roster itself to stop changing.** The previous fix judged a settled roster by edit timestamps, but the roster AutoDuty builds is driven through the monster notebook, whose selection writes never register as edits — so the timestamp stayed at screen-open while the build was still adding picks, and the correction still fired mid-build, where AutoDuty's continuing build and its confirm passes removed the added rows. The correction is now due only once the selected roster has been unchanged for 1.5 seconds — what the plugin sees every frame — never on an empty roster, and it still re-arms after any later AutoDuty write. The screen log's roster needfix line now also carries the age of the last edit (`adedit=`), the roster's quiet time (`adstb=`) and the selected count (`flutes=`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
